statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across 163 ant genomes, 145 of them newly sequenced, genome rearrangements were extensive and correlated with speciation rates.
statements.evidence: Comparative analyses of 163 ant genomes, including newly generated whole-genome sequences of 145 ant species, reveal extensive genome rearrangements correlated with speciation rates.
statements.note: The abstract reports that analyses of 163 ant genomes, including 145 newly sequenced species, revealed extensive rearrangements correlated with speciation rates.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The newly confirmed regulators of ant caste development determine caste mainly by altering DNA methylation.
statements.evidence: Previously uncharacterized genetic regulators of caste development were confirmed by functional experiments.
statements.note: The abstract says new caste regulators were confirmed experimentally but gives no molecular mechanism for how they act, DNA methylation or otherwise.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the common ancestor of ants, gene families for digestion, chemoreception, endocrine signaling and cuticular hydrocarbon synthesis expanded.
statements.evidence: Gene families related to digestion, endocrine signaling, cuticular hydrocarbon synthesis, and chemoreception expanded in the ant ancestor
statements.note: The abstract states that gene families in these four categories expanded in the ant ancestor.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Syntenic blocks preserved across ants are enriched for co-expressed genes involved in basal metabolism and caste differentiation.
statements.evidence: Meanwhile, conserved syntenic blocks are enriched with co-expressed genes involved in basal metabolism and caste differentiation.
statements.note: The abstract reports that conserved syntenic blocks are enriched with co-expressed genes for basal metabolism and caste differentiation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In a tetraploid Oryza, recently arisen paralogous genes are implicated in tolerating submergence in seawater.
statements.evidence: recent paralogues of a tetraploid Oryza are implicated in tolerance of seawater submergence
statements.note: The abstract states that recent paralogues of a tetraploid Oryza are implicated in tolerance of seawater submergence.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Sampling 363 grasses from all 12 subfamilies, the study detected nine more whole-genome duplications than had previously been recognised.
statements.evidence: Here we present phylogenomic/phylotranscriptomic analyses of 363 grasses covering all 12 subfamilies and report nine previously unknown whole-genome duplications.
statements.note: The abstract reports nine previously unknown whole-genome duplications from analyses of 363 grasses covering all 12 subfamilies.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rho duplicates retained differently among grass subfamilies include SPIRAL1, tied to rapid cell elongation in Bambusoideae, and CK2β, tied to cold responses in Pooideae.
statements.evidence: rho duplicates showing differential retention among subfamilies include those with functions in environmental adaptations or morphogenesis, including ACOT for aquatic environments (Oryzoideae), CK2β for cold responses (Pooideae), SPIRAL1 for rapid cell elongation (Bambusoideae)
statements.note: The abstract lists CK2β for cold responses in Pooideae and SPIRAL1 for rapid cell elongation in Bambusoideae among the differentially retained rho duplicates.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The rho whole-genome duplication shared by grasses took place roughly 70 million years ago.
statements.evidence: Poaceae members shared a whole-genome duplication called rho.
statements.note: The abstract says all Poaceae share the rho duplication but gives no date for it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: On a rearrangement index measured against the last common bilaterian ancestor, leeches and earthworms rank among the most rearranged genomes sampled so far.
statements.evidence: compared to the last common ancestor of bilaterians, leeches and earthworms have among the most highly rearranged genomes of any currently sampled species
statements.note: The abstract states that, relative to the bilaterian last common ancestor, leeches and earthworms have among the most highly rearranged genomes of any sampled species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among 23 chromosome-level annelid genomes, those of the Clitellata, which include leeches and earthworms, were completely scrambled, whereas many other annelid lineages kept the ancestral bilaterian arrangement.
statements.evidence: using 23 chromosome-level annelid genomes. We find that while many annelid lineages have maintained the conserved bilaterian genome structure, the Clitellata, a group containing leeches and earthworms, possesses completely scrambled genomes.
statements.note: The abstract reports that in its 23-genome analysis the Clitellata have completely scrambled genomes while many annelid lineages maintain the conserved bilaterian structure.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Transposable element activity drove the scrambling of leech and earthworm genomes.
statements.evidence: genome rearrangement can occur both in a gradual, stepwise fashion, or rapid, all-encompassing changes over short evolutionary timescales
statements.note: The abstract describes the tempo of genome rearrangement but names no cause for it, transposable elements included.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Bilaterian genomes fall into high- and low-rearrangement classes, largely depending on whether chromosome fission events have occurred.
statements.evidence: We further show that bilaterian genomes can be classified into two distinct categories-high and low rearrangement-largely influenced by the presence or absence, respectively, of chromosome fission events.
statements.note: The abstract states that the high- and low-rearrangement categories are largely influenced by the presence or absence, respectively, of chromosome fission events.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The resilience of Klebsormidiophyceae in harsh terrestrial habitats is a consequence of their filamentous body plan.
statements.evidence: Klebsormidiophyceae can exhibit filamentous body plans and display remarkable resilience as colonizers of terrestrial habitats.
statements.note: The abstract mentions both filamentous body plans and terrestrial resilience but does not link one causally to the other.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Built on 845 loci, the new phylogenomic framework assigns the six Klebsormidiophyceae genera to three newly defined orders, with a deep split dated to over 830 million years ago.
statements.evidence: Using an analysis built on 845 loci and sophisticated mixture models, we establish a phylogenomic framework, dividing the six distinct genera of Klebsormidiophyceae in a novel three-order system, with a deep divergence more than 830 million years ago.
statements.note: The abstract reports an 845-locus framework dividing the six genera into a novel three-order system with a deep divergence more than 830 million years ago.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study provides evidence placing the first multicellular streptophytes at around one billion years ago.
statements.evidence: We provide evidence that the first multicellular streptophytes likely lived about a billion years ago.
statements.note: The abstract states that the first multicellular streptophytes likely lived about a billion years ago.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Ancestral-state reconstructions point to repeated shifts between land and water, with stem Klebsormidiales colonizing land earlier than embryophytes.
statements.evidence: an evolutionary history of multiple transitions between terrestrial-aquatic habitats, with stem Klebsormidiales having conquered land earlier than embryophytes
statements.note: The abstract's ancestral-state reconstructions suggest multiple terrestrial-aquatic transitions, with stem Klebsormidiales conquering land earlier than embryophytes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Distinct brackish basins shared numerous species, but populations within each species were clearly separated geographically.
statements.evidence: In contrast, distinct brackish basins cohosted numerous species, but their intraspecific population structures displayed clear signs of geographic separation.
statements.note: The abstract reports that brackish basins cohosted many species whose intraspecific population structures showed clear geographic separation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Cross-biome transitions happened more often in Proteobacteria than in other bacterial phyla.
statements.evidence: We further identified the most recent cross-biome transitions, which were rare, ancient, and most commonly directed toward the brackish biome.
statements.note: The abstract describes how rare, old and directed the transitions were but does not compare their frequency among bacterial phyla.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Average nucleotide identity comparisons of 11,248 metagenome-assembled genomes showed that bacterial species were rarely shared between biomes.
statements.evidence: quality-filtered metagenome-assembled genomes (11,248). Average nucleotide identity analyses showed that bacterial species rarely existed in multiple biomes.
statements.note: The abstract states that, across 11,248 genomes, average nucleotide identity analyses showed bacterial species rarely existed in multiple biomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Moving between biomes went along with systematic changes in proteome amino acid composition and isoelectric point distribution that evolved over millions of years.
statements.evidence: Transitions were accompanied by systematic changes in amino acid composition and isoelectric point distributions of inferred proteomes, which evolved over millions of years
statements.note: The abstract reports that transitions were accompanied by systematic changes in amino acid composition and isoelectric points of inferred proteomes that evolved over millions of years.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study detected 19 separate amplifications of SNBP genes, and these took place preferentially on sex chromosomes.
statements.evidence: We found 19 independent SNBP gene amplification events that occurred preferentially on sex chromosomes.
statements.note: The abstract reports 19 independent SNBP gene amplification events that occurred preferentially on sex chromosomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with ancient SNBP genes, evolutionarily young ones were more often critical for fertility.
statements.evidence: Unexpectedly, evolutionarily young SNBP genes are more likely to be critical for fertility than ancient, conserved SNBP genes.
statements.note: The abstract states that young SNBP genes are more likely than ancient, conserved ones to be critical for fertility.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Loss of CG30056 loosens chromatin packaging in Drosophila melanogaster sperm.
statements.evidence: For example, CG30056 is dispensable for male fertility despite being one of three SNBP genes universally retained in Drosophila species.
statements.note: The abstract only reports that CG30056 is dispensable for male fertility; it says nothing about sperm chromatin packaging without it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the montium group, SNBP genes that are retained elsewhere were lost, coinciding with a fusion between the X and Y chromosomes.
statements.evidence: Conversely, the montium group of Drosophila species lost otherwise-conserved SNBP genes, coincident with an X-Y chromosomal fusion.
statements.note: The abstract states that the montium group lost otherwise-conserved SNBP genes, coincident with an X-Y chromosomal fusion.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Some early-diverging members of Amorphea lost one or both flagella, while breviates and apusomonads kept the ancestral biflagellate condition.
statements.evidence: Although breviates and apusomonads retained the ancestral biflagellate state, some early-diverging Amorphea lost one or both flagella
statements.note: The abstract states that breviates and apusomonads retained the ancestral biflagellate state whereas some early-diverging Amorphea lost one or both flagella.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The biflagellate common ancestor of Opimoda lived roughly one billion years ago.
statements.evidence: we infer an opimodan biflagellate ancestor with an excavate-like feeding groove, which ancyromonads subsequently lost
statements.note: The abstract infers the traits of the opimodan ancestor but gives no date for it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The analyses recovered Opimoda as monophyletic, with CRuMs placed as the sister group of Amorphea.
statements.evidence: Our findings support the monophyly of Opimoda, with CRuMs being sister to the Amorphea
statements.note: The abstract states that the findings support the monophyly of Opimoda with CRuMs sister to the Amorphea.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: New transcriptomes were obtained from 14 apusomonads, 7 ancyromonads and one cultured Mediterranean strain of Meteora sporadica.
statements.evidence: Here, we sequenced transcriptomes of poorly studied flagellates 23 , 24 (14 apusomonads, 25 , 26 7 ancyromonads, 27 and 1 cultured Mediterranean strain of Meteora sporadica 17 )
statements.note: The abstract lists newly sequenced transcriptomes from 14 apusomonads, 7 ancyromonads and 1 cultured Mediterranean strain of Meteora sporadica.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Following the triplication, the mangrove Sonneratia underwent extensive rearrangement of its chromosomes.
statements.evidence: Sonneratia, adapting mangrove habitats, experienced extensive chromosome rearrangements post-WGT.
statements.note: The abstract states that Sonneratia, adapting to mangrove habitats, experienced extensive chromosome rearrangements after the whole-genome triplication.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Roughly 64 million years ago, during a period of dramatic global climate change, the shared ancestor of Sonneratia alba and Lagerstroemia speciosa underwent a whole-genome triplication.
statements.evidence: Their common ancestor has experienced a whole-genome triplication (WGT) approximately 64 million years ago coinciding with a period of dramatic global climate change.
statements.note: The abstract dates the whole-genome triplication in the common ancestor of the two species to about 64 million years ago, coinciding with dramatic global climate change.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genes kept from the whole-genome triplication have become divergent in both sequence and expression.
statements.evidence: We observe the WGT retentions display sequence and expression divergence, suggesting potential neo- and sub-functionalization.
statements.note: The abstract reports that genes retained from the triplication display sequence and expression divergence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Lagerstroemia speciosa retained fewer triplicated gene copies than Sonneratia alba.
statements.evidence: Strong selection acting on three-copy retentions indicates adaptive value in response to new environments.
statements.note: The abstract discusses three-copy retentions and the selection acting on them but never compares retention between the two species.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Vertically inherited genes contributed more than horizontally acquired genes to the pathogenicity of Armillaria.
statements.evidence: Overall, this study details how evolution knitted together horizontally and vertically inherited genes in complex adaptive traits of plant biomass degradation and pathogenicity in important fungal pathogens.
statements.note: The abstract says horizontally and vertically inherited genes were combined in these traits but does not compare their contributions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Horizontal gene transfer offers an explanation for the unusual, soft rot-like way in which Armillaria decays wood.
statements.evidence: provides an explanation for their unusual, soft rot-like wood decay strategy
statements.note: The abstract states that horizontal gene transfer provides an explanation for the unusual soft rot-like wood decay strategy of Armillaria.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Through 124 horizontal gene transfer events, Armillaria species picked up no fewer than 1,025 genes, most of them from Ascomycota.
statements.evidence: Armillaria species, in addition to gene duplications and de novo gene origins, acquired at least 1,025 genes via 124 horizontal gene transfer events, primarily from Ascomycota.
statements.note: The abstract reports that Armillaria acquired at least 1,025 genes via 124 horizontal gene transfer events, primarily from Ascomycota.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Two newly described small secreted proteins that are induced during pathogenesis triggered necrosis in planta.
statements.evidence: two novel conserved pathogenicity-induced small secreted proteins, which induced necrosis in planta
statements.note: The abstract reports two novel pathogenicity-induced small secreted proteins that induced necrosis in planta.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Nematodes bearing a stomatostylet evolved from fungal-feeding ancestors.
statements.evidence: All stomatostylet-bearing nematodes are proposed to have originated ~305 Ma, corresponding to the transition from the Devonian to the Permian period.
statements.note: The abstract dates the origin of stomatostylet-bearing nematodes but says nothing about what their ancestors fed on.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Contrary to its placement in previous studies, the genus Thornia fell outside both Dorylaimina and Nygolaimina.
statements.evidence: The genus Thornia is placed outside of Dorylaimina and Nygolaimina, disagreeing with its position in previous studies.
statements.note: The abstract places Thornia outside Dorylaimina and Nygolaimina, in disagreement with its position in previous studies.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Trichinella and Trichuris were estimated to share a common ancestor around 202 million years ago, considerably later than previously proposed.
statements.evidence: The genera Trichinella and Trichuris are inferred to have shared a common ancestor approximately 202 millions of years ago (Ma), a considerably later period than previously suggested.
statements.note: The abstract infers a Trichinella-Trichuris common ancestor about 202 Ma, a considerably later period than previously suggested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The subclass Enoplia was recovered as the sister group to all other nematodes, in line with previously published phylogenies.
statements.evidence: The subclass Enoplia is placed as a sister group to the rest of Nematoda, agreeing with previously published phylogenies.
statements.note: The abstract places Enoplia as sister to the rest of Nematoda, in agreement with previously published phylogenies.
